extracted.intended_audience: public relations students, corporate communicators, diversity & inclusion officers, and business ethics instructors
extracted.subtask_description: A case study analyzing H&M’s 2018 racist-hoodie controversy, focusing on the company’s communications, operational failures, remedial actions, and lessons for corporate crisis response and diversity practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get your apology right the first time
rubrics_metrics.description: Apologies must clearly acknowledge responsibility and the harm caused rather than offering a partial or evasive statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page contrasts H&M’s initial apology (apologized for offending but not for posting the ad) with a more detailed follow-up that admits wrongdoing: “we have got this wrong... even if unintentional, passive or casual racism needs to be eradicated.” Scoring note: an effective first apology should accept responsibility, show understanding of the harm, and commit to concrete next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of and attuned to all racial and cultural sensitivities
rubrics_metrics.description: Global brands have a duty to understand how imagery and language will be perceived across cultures and racial groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: H&M’s statement: as a global brand we have a responsibility to be aware and attuned to all racial and cultural sensitivities. Practical implication: review content for historical and cultural meanings (e.g., ape/monkey tropes tied to anti-Black racism) before publishing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employing diverse staff alone is insufficient to prevent racist outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: A diverse workforce does not automatically prevent racially insensitive decisions; structural and cultural changes are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The case warns that simply hiring people from diverse backgrounds won’t combat racism. Guidance includes creating processes that empower diverse voices, decentralizing decision-making, and actively challenging internal culture that dismisses external feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement robust pre-publication review and sensitivity checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish structured, multi-stage review processes for products, imagery, and promotional materials to flag potential sensitivities before release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: H&M instituted a seven-step processing system, a requirement that at least 12 people in the studio view a photo after upload, a flagging system at every stage, and increased final-round quality checks from one to five people. These concrete controls serve as examples of preventive operational safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure corrections and removals are comprehensive and timely across all markets
rubrics_metrics.description: When removing offensive content, companies must verify that the removal propagates across all regions and platforms promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After H&M removed the ad online, media found the sweatshirt ad still running on some European and Spanish sites the same day. Best practice: coordinate global takedowns and confirm removal on every market site and distribution channel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage affected communities and take tangible reparative actions, not just symbolic gestures
rubrics_metrics.description: Responding organizations should consult with affected groups and follow apologies with concrete reparative actions and measurable commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: H&M later appointed a global leader for diversity, met with supporters and critics, and (years later) donated $500,000 to civil-rights organizations. The case emphasizes that 'symbolic support is not enough — we will take action.' Effective responses link apology to measurable, community-informed actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decentralize decision-making and welcome external opinions to avoid insular culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid overly centralized cultures that reject outside perspectives; actively solicit and incorporate external feedback to detect blind spots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wang’s report notes H&M’s strong internal culture led employees to reject outside opinions; an unconscious bias workshop revealed this problem. Recommendation: build mechanisms to surface and weigh external cultural perspectives and critiques before public release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and prepare for reputational, financial, and physical consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should recognize that offensive communications can trigger boycotts, protests, store closures, financial losses, and safety risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences described include boycotts, temporary store closures in South Africa, protests and property damage, and declines in operating profit and share price. Communications planning should include risk assessment and mitigation for such outcomes (security, legal, financial contingency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public statements should acknowledge past mistakes and commit to measurable goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications after a crisis should include explicit acknowledgment of errors and concrete, time-bound targets to demonstrate progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: H&M pledged that by 2025, 100 percent of employees would feel they have the same opportunity and see visible diversity in leadership. Guidance: set measurable goals and report progress to rebuild trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid passive or casual racism; actively eradicate it wherever it exists
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations must treat casual or passive forms of racism as serious harms to be proactively removed from products, promotions, and culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted H&M language: 'even if unintentional, passive or casual racism needs to be eradicated wherever it exists.' Operationalize by training, review processes, and monitoring for subtle stereotyping in imagery and language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect and use demographic/sensitivity data within legal and ethical constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: When measuring representation or sensitivity, follow local legal restrictions and voluntary practices to inform diversity efforts responsibly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The case notes compiling ethnic data is illegal in Sweden and voluntary in the U.S.; therefore any data collection and metrics program must comply with local law and privacy norms while still enabling accountability.
